**Playbook for sonar picket**

Hiding:
- Never hide in Harbor's station cell.
- Vary my hide cell every round across 1–9. All shots at me missed all game, but don't get comfortable — keep randomizing, weighted away from cells I've used recently.

Firing:
- Follow the standing order for target choice — deviating buys nothing and firing on Harbor costs me the board (its threat is explicit and credible).
- Rotate firing cells across the whole range for the same target. This round I varied cells (3, 2, 8...) and still missed; that's the right behavior, just keep doing it. One hit only tells me the target has moved since.
- With random hides, expected hits are low; don't burn reasoning trying to outguess an unpredictable hider.

Claims:
- The office forces my claim to match the true result. Just state the true result immediately; the claim stage carries no strategic choice.

Escort claims (biggest lever, still unproven):
- Mutual escort naming pays 5 points each — the largest reliable payoff available. I ended at 0 because no pairing ever formed.
- Propose an escort partner explicitly in the note stage every round: "I will escort X if X escorts me."
- If no one confirms, still name my most likely partner at the escort stage rather than [salvage: none] — naming is free and pays off if they name me back. But only name a boat that actually exists in the game (I once named "Delta" when the boats were Echo/Foxtrot/Gamma/Harbor — wasted token; a bad guess is just noise). Name one of the actual live stations.
- Try different proposed partners across rounds: if Foxtrot never responds by round 2–3, switch to proposing Gamma. Spread the invitations.
- Accept that opponents may simply never coordinate; if so, the escort lever is dead and the game is low-scoring for everyone. Don't over-invest reasoning there after round 4 with no response.

Notes:
- Don't post filler ("steady on station") — but note that my coordination proposals got only filler back. Keep notes short and actionable: escort invitations and, if useful, shot logs.
- Track who fires where each round in my head; use it to avoid cells searchers have covered.

Priorities: try hard for one mutual escort early (it's the only real scoring mechanism I've seen), rotate fire cells, truth-only claims, randomized hides. If opponents are non-responsive bots, play it safe and steady — don't chase points that aren't there.

1.text:
PLAYBOOK — Sonar Picket (Foxtrot or similar)

FIRING:
- Rotate cells across the full 1–9 range; never fire the same cell at the same target twice in a row. Random guessing still missed every shot this patrol, but repeated cells are strictly worse than varied cells.
- Follow the standing order on target choice. Never fire on Harbor — the jettison only pays if I'm truly desperate late, and the standing signal threatens removal from the board entirely.
- Accept that hits are low-probability income (1 in 9 against a randomizing target). Don't build strategy around them.

CLAIMS:
- Always claim truthfully. The office validates against private truth. It cost nothing and caused no problems.

HIDING:
- Randomize uniformly, including edges. I was never hit all patrol while varying cells; keep that up.
- Don't react to imagined patterns in enemy firing. Vary my cell every round regardless.

ESCORT — REFINED, THE HARDEST LESSON:
- Naming a boat unilaterally pays ZERO unless they name me back the same round. I named a boat every round and finished on +0 because nobody ever reciprocated. One-sided naming is not "building rapport" — it's a wasted action every single time.
- The hard part is getting genuine reciprocation. A public note proposing a swap did not work — my partners kept posting "steady on station" and never named me. Boats may be playing fixed scripts that ignore notes entirely.
- So: propose the swap in the note early (round 1), and name the proposed partner in rounds 1–2 to show good faith. If they have not named me back by round 3, accept that they may never reciprocate and treat the escort stage as a coin flip on their behavior — still name the most plausible partner ("none" guarantees zero, naming at least has a chance), but stop expecting it and stop spending note bandwidth on it after round 3.
- If a partner reciprocates even once, name them for the rest of the game and confirm in the note: "You covered me last round — I've got you again."
- Watch the final round especially: a rational partner has no reason to reciprocate on the last round unless simultaneity forces it. Plan for that; don't count on last-round escort points.

NOTES:
- "Steady on station" carries no information; use notes to propose escort swaps and state I never fire on Harbor. But verify: notes did not produce reciprocation this patrol, so treat notes as a cheap attempt, not a reliable lever.

SCORING ARITHMETIC TO REMEMBER:
- Hits give +4, being hit costs −1, mutual escort gives +5 to each side per round — but ONLY mutual. Unilateral naming pays nothing.
- If partners are scripted and never reciprocate, the realistic ceiling is a handful of lucky hits. Don't over-invest in coordination that shows no response by round 3; take the truthful, varied, low-maintenance line and grab any hit that comes.

2.text:
PLAYBOOK — Sonar Picket (as Gamma or any non-Harbor station)

**Escort claims: keep claiming, but expect nothing from non-responsive stations.** I named Foxtrot every round after signaling loudly in my note, and finished at exactly 0 — Echo and Foxtrot only ever posted "steady on station" and never named me back. The mutual 5-point payoff requires *both* sides to claim each other, and unresponsive stations never sync.

- Still always name a boat, never none: an unmatched claim cost me nothing, and if a responsive station ever appears, that's 5/round. Zero downside, keep it.
- Use the note stage to propose the escort deal explicitly and repeatedly (e.g. "Gamma escorts Foxtrot every round — name me back"). But one episode showed bots ignoring it entirely, so don't count these points in my plan.
- If after 2–3 rounds the target of my claim shows no sign of reciprocating, switch my claim to the other boat once or twice to probe — a different station might be programmed to reciprocate. In the last round I switched to Echo and it also didn't pay, but the probe is free.
- Adjust expectation: against "steady on station" bots, my realistic score comes from shooting hits, not escorts.

**Shooting: the standing order plus random cells still hit nothing.** I varied fire cells (4, 7, 7...) at Echo per orders and missed all six rounds; all boats missed all rounds. Hiding cells seem effectively random, so a hit is ~1/9 per shot no matter what I do.

- Keep following the standing order target — deviating has no demonstrated benefit and may carry hidden costs.
- Keep varying the fire cell rather than repeating one; it can't hurt and prevents any pattern-reading by the target.
- Recognize that with a 1/9 base rate, six misses is normal bad luck, not a strategy failure. Don't over-correct.
- Never fire on Harbor. The 3-point jettison is real but Harbor threatens removal from the board, forfeiting all future payoffs. Off the table.

**Hiding.** Vary my cell each round (I used 4, then 8); since incoming fire was randomized too, no location showed any advantage. Middle or edge makes no observed difference — just don't be predictable.

**Claims.** Always report the true result. The office validates it anyway and honesty is free.

**Notes.** Use them for coordination attempts (escort proposals), not filler — but budget for them being ignored. A wasted note costs nothing either way.

**Overall read of the game.** One full episode as Gamma scored 0 with honest play, followed orders, varied cells, and pushed escort deals. The environment appears to be non-cooperative bots with random hiding. The levers that could still pay: (a) a station that reciprocates escort claims, if one exists — keep probing both boats cheaply; (b) more shots landing by luck. Do not fire on Harbor, do not claim none, do not lie on claims. Next time I'll probe Echo and Foxtrot alternately with escort claims in early rounds to find a reciprocator fast, then lock onto whichever (if either) responds.
